reason: For a legal input (distinct starter ids), KeepsPrefix gives r ++ t. AddsOnlyAbsent and AddsAllAbsent fix the set of new ids to the absent starters, and SameRow fixes id, adapter and model. KeepsStarterOrder fixes the order and rules out duplicates, because a sublist of a distinct-id list has distinct ids. NewDisabled, LockedDisabled and EnableKeepsState fix enabled in every case (enable off, locked adapter, enable on with unlocked adapter). So each design that passes gives the same registry as ref.
